memory_candidates.content: When a plan phase's sole remaining criterion is a passive/probabilistic production event whose emission mechanism has already been independently function-verified (e.g. via a sandboxed harness) but simply hasn't yet coincided with the right live timing window, prefer closing that phase as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with a documented Reasoned Exclusion over leaving it [PARTIAL] indefinitely. The admission test's 'no residual work' condition is satisfied when nothing needs to be scheduled or retried -- the event will fire naturally as a side effect of ordinary system operation, which is a fundamentally different situation from a phase that is genuinely stuck or incomplete.

When re-verifying a stale handoff's claimed blockers, run the exact independently-verifiable commands the handoff itself specifies (jq queries against deployed settings.json, doc-lint gate invocations, event-type counts in the JSONL store) rather than trusting the handoff's prose. A handoff written even ~12 hours earlier can be significantly stale if external regeneration or accumulated usage occurred in the interim -- in this case the handoff's 'zero artifact-category events, zero session_stop events' claim was directly contradicted by live re-checking (26 and 70 respectively).
